subsystems.name: Corpus ingestion
subsystems.role: gathers and parses scientific text and structured data from many different fields.

subsystems.name: Knowledge graph
subsystems.role: stores concepts and their relationships as a queryable network with provenance.

subsystems.name: Semantic embedding model
subsystems.role: places concepts from different fields in a shared vector space so similar ideas sit close together.

subsystems.name: Link discovery engine
subsystems.role: finds missing or non-obvious connections between distant domains.

subsystems.name: Hypothesis ranker and explainer
subsystems.role: orders candidate links by novelty and evidence, and explains them in plain language.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a cross-domain corpus
buildSteps.detail: Collect open-access papers, patents and structured datasets from several fields, normalising formats and licences.

buildSteps.title: Extract entities and relations
buildSteps.detail: Run natural-language processing to pull out concepts such as genes, materials or methods, and the relationships stated in text.

buildSteps.title: Align vocabularies
buildSteps.detail: Map synonyms and field-specific terms onto shared identifiers using existing ontologies, so that a term in one field can be compared with a term in another.

buildSteps.title: Build the knowledge graph
buildSteps.detail: Store nodes, edges and their provenance in a graph database that supports fast traversal and querying.

buildSteps.title: Train semantic and graph models
buildSteps.detail: Learn vector representations and link-prediction models that generalise across domains rather than memorising one field.

buildSteps.title: Generate candidate links
buildSteps.detail: Apply algorithms to propose edges or paths that are absent from the graph but statistically plausible given the surrounding structure.

buildSteps.title: Rank and explain candidates
buildSteps.detail: Score each candidate by novelty, evidence strength and coherence, then produce a short human-readable rationale.

buildSteps.title: Validate and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Test top candidates with domain experts or bench experiments, and feed the results back to retrain and improve the models.

prerequisites.why: the system must read and parse millions of documents across fields.
fields use different vocabularies, and alignment is often incomplete or contested.

prerequisites.tech: Graph neural networks and link prediction
prerequisites.why: these work well within a domain but are less reliable across very different ones.
they can connect ideas but may hallucinate and lack grounding in verified data.
human judgement is still needed to separate a real cross-domain insight from a plausible-looking coincidence.

pathway.milestone: literature-based discovery tools that suggest cross-domain links from published text
pathway.unlocks: faster hypothesis generation in areas such as drug repurposing and materials search.

pathway.milestone: domain-focused synthesis agents that combine text, data and simulations to propose testable hypotheses
pathway.unlocks: more reliable leads with fewer false positives.

pathway.milestone: general cross-domain agents that autonomously design and run in-silico experiments
pathway.unlocks: rapid exploration of very large search spaces across several fields at once.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop discovery where AI proposes, robots test and results feed back automatically
pathway.unlocks: accelerated science with less human bottleneck in routine experimentation.
